days.label: Travel
days.plan: Depart Seattle. Flight details are private data — see the imported private file.
days.tiredDaySummary: No walking target. Pack is cabin baggage.

days.label: Arrival
days.plan: Arrive Narita. Immigration, pocket WiFi, cash, train to Tokyo, sleep. Times, order numbers and the hotel are private data — see the imported private file.
days.tiredDaySummary: Ordinary arrival walking only. Favour daylight and a normal bedtime.

safetyNotes: Urban traffic and crowding, not exposure. The real risk today is doing more than 17.7 km because it feels easy.

REVERSIBLE THIS MORNING. This walk was moved from Oct 21 to Oct 20 so a rest day falls AFTER the first walking day instead of before it. If the flight was late or the night was bad, swap it back: museum today, walk tomorrow. Both dates are open museum days in the same rotation, the hotel is the same either way, and no booking is affected. Decide at breakfast, not in advance.
verificationTasks: Measure the actual pedestrian line on a GPX, not the post-station table.
Confirm the Kawasaki endpoint and its relationship to the hotel.
days.label: Walk 1 — Nihonbashi to Kawasaki
days.plan: Nihonbashi → Shinagawa → Kawasaki-juku.
days.startLightGuidance: Start at first light if the body offers it. Tokyo is sixteen hours ahead of Seattle, so on the first morning 06:00 here reads as early afternoon at home: alert, and the crash comes at about 15:00 local. Thirteen miles started at 06:30 finishes inside that window. This is the one day the jet lag is an asset, and it is gone by Walk 3.
days.sleepBaseNote: Not the walk endpoint. The Tokyo arrival hotel is booked through the morning of Oct 22, so tonight means riding back in from Hatchonawate. Tomorrow is a rest day in the same bed; the return to this point is on Oct 22. This is the one day whose bed is behind the walker rather than ahead.
days.tiredDaySummary: Short day by design. Rail parallels the whole line. Stop early rather than borrowing against tomorrow.

verificationTasks: Open the Asoview ticket in the app at the hotel, not at the gate: it is phone-only, needs a live connection, and the seller warns some handsets cannot display it.
Check feet, socks, shoes and pack fit against what the first walking day produced. Tokyo is the best place on the route to replace any of them, and Fujisawa and Odawara are not.
days.label: Tokyo rest and the Hiroshige exhibition
days.plan: Hiroshige exhibition at the Tokyo National Museum, Honkan Room A. Feet, pack and shoes reviewed after the first walking day. Takkyubin send to Hamamatsu if the chain is confirmed.
days.startLightGuidance: No mileage target. Museum opens 09:30; the ticket needs no time slot.
days.tiredDaySummary: The point of this day is diagnosis, not rest. Whatever the first thirteen miles revealed, today is when it gets fixed.

days.label: Walk 2 — Kawasaki to Fujisawa
days.plan: Kawasaki → Kanagawa → Hodogaya → Totsuka → Fujisawa-juku.
days.startLightGuidance: First full pavement day. Feet and pack govern pace, not the clock.
days.tiredDaySummary: Dense rail. Stopping anywhere is cheap today.

safetyNotes: Arriving at Odawara tired is a legitimate reason to spend a recovery token here rather than start Hakone short of sleep.
days.label: Walk 3 — Fujisawa to Odawara
days.plan: Fujisawa → Hiratsuka → Oiso → Odawara-juku.
days.startLightGuidance: Finish below Hakone. Do not borrow against the mountain day.
days.tiredDaySummary: Finish at Odawara. Tomorrow is the hard one.

safetyNotes: Hakone Pass IC on the west slope: Route 1, Hakone Shindo, the old-road approaches and the Ashinoko Skyline access converge. The pedestrian margin is green paint on a highway shoulder. There is no curb and no barrier. Paint is not protection.
Published accounts describe several hundred metres of Route 1 without sidewalk plus an unprotected crossing near the Hakone Shindo merge.
This is one of the two lowest-rail-redundancy days on the route. Suzuka is the other.
verificationTasks: Check current trail notices for the Hiryu Falls nature trail and the restored west-slope old road within days of the crossing.
Map the Hakone Pass IC micro-route continuously: green-shoulder exposure, the old-road/golf-road loop, and the Yasuragi-no-Mori wooded connector reported May 2026.
Confirm east-side and west-side bus timetables as the actual mid-crossing exit.
weatherSensitive: Hiryu Falls nature trail: Kanagawa Prefecture advises against use during or just after rain; sections are prone to crumbling.

Upper west-slope old road reopened 2026-03-30 after typhoon restoration; Kannami Town asks walkers to avoid it in rain and for several days after. Route 1 is the designated wet-weather detour — and Route 1 is where the shoulder problem is.
days.label: Walk 4 — Odawara over Hakone to Lake Ashi
days.plan: Odawara → Hakone-Yumoto → Hatajuku → (Hiryu Falls / Ashinoyu hybrid) → the Lake Ashi shore at Moto-Hakone, 1.20 km short of the Sekisho. Stops at the top: the climb without the descent.
days.terrain: Roughly 640 m of ascent on the east slope, much of it stone-paved trail, then a steep western descent.
days.elevationWarning: The largest single climb and descent on the route. Wet stone is the specific hazard, not the gradient.
days.startLightGuidance: First-light start. This is the day where losing two hours in the morning changes what is safe in the afternoon.
days.sleepBaseNote: Booked at the lake, which is why this day stops at the checkpoint instead of descending to Mishima. No railway crosses the historic pass: Odawara and Mishima are both Shinkansen stops, but a mid-crossing exit means reaching a trailhead or a bus stop, not a station.
days.tiredDaySummary: Biggest climb, worst shoulder, fewest trains. Start at first light. If the mountain is wet, the recovery token moves here — that is what it is for.

weatherSensitive: THE WEST SLOPE IS WALKED ON THIS DAY, not Walk 4. Kannami Town asks walkers to avoid the upper west-slope old road in rain and for several days after; it reopened 2026-03-30 after typhoon restoration. Route 1 is the designated wet-weather detour — and Route 1 is where the unresolved Hakone Pass IC shoulder problem is, so neither option is free. Decide before leaving Lake Ashi, where there is still a bed and a recovery token.
If Walk 4 was wet, this descent is the reason to spend the token rather than the climb.

ROUTE 1 IS NOT AN UNCONDITIONAL DETOUR. The Route 1 section through Kannami — 茨ケ平 to 枯木, 103.0–106.7 kp, 3.7 km — is a rainfall-regulated stretch that CLOSES at 250 mm cumulative rainfall, with recorded closures in 2007, 2011 and 2012. That is typhoon rain rather than ordinary rain, so it is a tail risk, not a daily one — but it is the same ground the wet-weather detour sends you to, so in genuinely heavy weather both options can be shut and the answer is the train from Mishima, not a third road.
days.label: Walk 5 — Lake Ashi to Fuji
days.plan: Lake Ashi shore → Hakone Sekisho (first thing, in the morning, when it is open) → Hakone Pass → Mishima → Numazu → Hara → past Yoshiwara-juku to the Fuji hotel. Starts at 725 m and descends the west slope.
days.terrain: Long descent off the pass, then sustained pavement.
days.elevationWarning: Opens with 5.5 km of unpaved trail down the west slope — the largest single stretch of unpaved ground on the route — on cold legs, first thing. Wet stone is the hazard, not the gradient, exactly as on Walk 4.
days.sleepBaseNote: The route passes 62 m from the door, so the day ends at the bed rather than walking to it. One of the three longest days, with Walk 10 and Walk 6 — and within 50 m of Walk 6, which is too close to rank honestly.
days.startLightGuidance: Opens with the Hakone west descent on cold legs. The descent, not the distance, is what to pace.
days.tiredDaySummary: Shortened to Yoshiwara so the Lake Ashi remainder spreads onto Walks 6 and 7 instead of landing here. The Tokaido Main Line parallels most of it, so stopping early and riding in is cheap.

verificationTasks: Confirm the Satta Pass path is open; it is the one view worth rescheduling for.
weatherSensitive: Satta Pass viewpoint is weather-dependent and the reason to be there.

About 900 m of the descent west of Satta is unpaved trail — the only unpaved ground on this day. If the weather has already taken the view away, the coastal corridor through Yui and Okitsu is the alternative and the Tokaido Main Line parallels it the whole way.
days.label: Walk 6 — Fuji over Satta to Shizuoka
days.plan: Fuji → Kambara → Yui → Satta Pass → Okitsu → Ejiri → past Fuchu-juku to the Shizuoka hotel, 1,091 m further on.
days.terrain: Two short climbs (Satta, Utsunoya) inside a long pavement day.
days.elevationWarning: Modest elevation. Satta is the only climb; Mariko and Utsunoya moved to Walk 7 when the endpoint came back to Fuchu.
days.startLightGuidance: Early start. The research stops, not the distance, are what will eat the daylight.
days.sleepBaseNote: The route passes 26 m from the door. Fuchu-juku and JR Shizuoka Station are both passed 1,091 m earlier.
days.tiredDaySummary: One climb, then a long flat run into Shizuoka. Rail is dense — moving the endpoint costs little.

safetyNotes: Utsunoya: repair work is scheduled during FY2026. Confirm the tunnel is open as a walking route shortly before the crossing.
verificationTasks: Recheck Utsunoya tunnel status against Shizuoka City and Fujieda City notices in October 2026.
weatherSensitive: Utsunoya is a choice, not a hazard: the traced line goes OVER the pass on the old footway, and the Meiji tunnel runs beneath it and rejoins the same road at both ends. Paved and lit against an unpaved mountain path, at almost no cost in distance. In heavy rain take the tunnel — but confirm it is open first, because FY2026 repair work could remove the option.
days.label: Walk 7 — Shizuoka over Utsunoya to Shimada
days.plan: Shizuoka → Fuchu-juku → Mariko → Utsunoya → Okabe → Fujieda → Shimada-juku.
days.terrain: Utsunoya early, then tea-country hills after the Oi River crossing.
days.sleepBaseNote: Lodging 41 m off the route and 141 m from the Shimada-juku finish — walked in, no transfer. Desk closes at midnight and there is no after-hours check-in. Walking on to Kanaya-juku instead is a day-of option: the route passes 15 m from that platform and one stop brings you back here, which takes 5.4 km off Walk 8.
days.tiredDaySummary: Shortest walking day after Walk 8b. Utsunoya early, then a steady run down to Shimada, where the bed is on the road. The Nissaka finish with its 6.7 km rural bus was dropped on 2026-09-24.

verificationTasks: Tenryu crossing: confirm which span carries the walkway and that the under-bridge approach is open. Verified in Street View 2026-09-13, not on the ground.
days.label: Walk 8 — Shimada to Iwata
days.plan: Shimada → Oi River → Kanaya → Sayo-no-Nakayama → Nissaka → Kakegawa → Fukuroi → Mitsuke → Iwata, 255.15 km. Rail three stops into the booked Hamamatsu bed.
days.terrain: Tea-country hills after the Oi River, then flat pavement.
days.sleepBase: Hamamatsu, three JR stops back from Iwata
days.sleepBaseNote: Iwata Station is 181 m off the route — the closest approach of any station between Kanaya and Hamamatsu. Stopping at the 25-mile mark instead leaves 900 m to the platform, so finish at 255.15 km, not later. Toyodacho (13.1 km left for Walk 8b) and Tenryugawa (5.2 km left) are the longer options if the legs are good.
days.startLightGuidance: The day the Shimada split was built for. Every exit from Kanaya west is on the JR Tokaido Main Line, so stopping short costs a train ride and nothing else — the Hamamatsu bed is booked for the following night too, and Walk 8b finishes whatever is left.
days.tiredDaySummary: Eighth walking day. Reach Iwata, ride in, sleep. Walk 8b carries the last 15.8 km into Hamamatsu in the morning.

verificationTasks: Tenryu crossing: confirm which span carries the walkway and that the under-bridge approach is open. Verified in Street View 2026-09-13, not on the ground.
days.label: Walk 8b — Iwata to Hamamatsu, part recovery
days.plan: Rail three stops back to Iwata, walk the last 15.8 km into Hamamatsu-juku, then laundry, feet, pack repairs, field-system check, and a private visit if it confirms.
days.terrain: Flat pavement, the Tenryu crossing in the middle.
days.sleepBaseNote: Same bed as the night before; nothing to move. Walk 9 starts on foot from it.
days.startLightGuidance: A half day, not a rest day, and it was not chosen — Shimada to Hamamatsu is 55.2 km and cannot be one day, so whatever Walk 8 leaves lands here. Finish the walking early enough that the recovery half actually happens.
days.tiredDaySummary: The recovery token is spent walking. If Walk 8 reached Tenryugawa instead of Iwata this is only 5.2 km and most of the day is yours.

safetyNotes: Verify pedestrian routing and legality across the Hamanako bridges before committing to the day.
verificationTasks: Confirm pedestrian access on every Hamanako bridge segment.
weatherSensitive: High wind on the exposed Hamanako bridges is a real stop condition. Rail parallels the whole crossing.
days.label: Walk 9 — Hamamatsu to Toyohashi
days.plan: Hamamatsu → Maisaka → Arai → Shirasuka → Futagawa → Yoshida/Toyohashi.
days.sleepBaseNote: The route passes 39 m from the door, 66 m from the Yoshida-juku finish — nearer than Toyohashi Station, which is 883 m away. Onsen on site. Call the property if arriving after 22:00.
days.tiredDaySummary: Wind, not distance, is the governing variable. Trains run alongside; a windy day is a train day.

days.label: Walk 10 — Toyohashi to Shin-Anjo
days.plan: Toyohashi → Goyu → Akasaka → Fujikawa → Okazaki → Toeicho crossing (Shin-Anjo).
days.sleepBaseNote: The bed is 579 m south of the road at the Toeicho signal, on a street that runs straight down to Shin-Anjo Station. That is the shortest hotel access on the route; finishing at Okazaki-juku instead meant 3.4 km to Okazaki Station.
days.startLightGuidance: No longer the light day it was. Extended past Okazaki to take six miles off Walk 11, which has to get back to Nagoya from Manba Ohashi.
days.tiredDaySummary: Flat, rail-dense, and longer than it used to be. Meitetsu runs beside the old road most of the way, so stopping early and riding the last stretch into Shin-Anjo costs little.

verificationTasks: Confirm the Kanayama hotel will hold a pack before check-in on Nov 1. The shape of this day rests on it.

Walk 12 carries the Manba stretch but was shortened to Ise-Asahi on 2026-09-16 and now runs 34.6 km, so the Kiso Three Rivers crossing no longer has a threshold to cross. Measure it anyway: it is the largest unmeasured distance on the route.
days.label: Walk 11 — Shin-Anjo to Iwatsuka
days.plan: Shin-Anjo → Chiryu → Narumi → Miya/Atsuta → Saya Kaido → Iwatsuka Station crossing.
days.sleepBaseNote: Two stations sit on this day. The line passes 191 m from Kanayama Station at 378.71 km — 16.4 mi in, and the hotel is there — so leave the pack at the hotel on the way past, room ready or not, and walk the last 3.0 mi unladen. It finishes 396 m from Iwatsuka Station: step off the road, Higashiyama line to Nagoya, one hop back to Kanayama. Nov 3 reverses it in about twenty minutes. Manba Ohashi, 1.91 km further west, was the finish until 2026-09-16; it has no station, so ending there meant walking that stretch twice or waiting on a bus.
days.tiredDaySummary: Nineteen miles, urban and rail-dense, the day before a rest day, and the pack only has to be carried for the first sixteen. Finishes at a subway entrance rather than a bridge.

days.label: Recovery 2 — Nagoya/Atsuta
days.plan: Recovery and research token before the western block.
days.sleepBaseNote: Movable toward the Suzuka gate if the forecast requires it.
days.tiredDaySummary: No mileage required. The least forgiving stages start tomorrow.

safetyNotes: Iwatsuka → Kameyama was dropped in the 2026-11-02 replan, with no make-up mileage.
Sort out tomorrow’s weather decision tonight: Suzuka is tomorrow.
days.label: Walk 12 — Kameyama to Ono-cho (train from Nagoya)
days.plan: JR from Nagoya on the Kansai Line to Kameyama; walk Kameyama-juku → Ono-cho. Replanned 2026-11-02: Iwatsuka → Kuwana → Yokkaichi → Kameyama is ridden, not walked.
days.startLightGuidance: No early start needed. The day exists to arrive rested at the foot of Suzuka. Kameyama Station is about 0.6 km from Kameyama-juku.
days.sleepBaseNote: The bed is about 250 m off the road. Check-in any time.
days.tiredDaySummary: Train, then about 3 mi of town walking to the hotel. Rest for Suzuka.

safetyNotes: Seki is the last easy train exit before the pass. There is no rail between Seki and Tsuchiyama.
Modern Route 1 runs through the Suzuka Tunnel below the pass; the old road climbs over the saddle as part of the Tokai Nature Trail. Those are different lines with different exposure.
verificationTasks: Confirm Tokai Nature Trail condition and any closures.
Confirm the daylight margin against an actual sunrise time, not an assumed one.
weatherSensitive: Cold and wind at the saddle. Put the midlayer and shell on before the descent, not after the sweat cools.
days.label: Walk 13 — Ono-cho over Suzuka to Minakuchi
days.plan: Ono-cho → Seki → Sakashita → Suzuka Pass → Tsuchiyama → Minakuchi-juku → the road point nearest the Minakuchi hotel, 2.7 km on. Moved to Wednesday on 2026-11-02 for the weather.
days.terrain: Forested Mie-side ascent to roughly 378 m, then the gentler Shiga-side descent.
days.elevationWarning: Modest in absolute height, but exposed, cool, and windy, and the Mie-side approach feels remote. Walking Tokyo-to-Kyoto makes the steep side the ascent.
days.startLightGuidance: First-light start and an explicit weather gate. Nothing stands between the bed and the road: the night before ends about 250 m off the Tokaido. The pass falls about 10.7 km in, after Seki and Sakashita. Climb it early.
days.sleepBaseNote: The bed is about 0.6 km off the road from this finish point. Check-in until midnight, no after-hours arrival.
days.tiredDaySummary: The mountain day: about 20.7 mi, low rail, first light, warm layers before the descent. Seki is the last easy exit.

weatherSensitive: The day most likely to be wet. Flat and beside the railway, so heavy rain means a train, not a risk.
days.label: Walk 14 — Minakuchi to Tehara
days.plan: Minakuchi → Mikumo → Ishibe → Tehara, 4.6 km before Kusatsu-juku. Replanned 2026-11-02: the expected wet day falls on the flat, rail-dense stretch.
days.terrain: Flat, beside the JR Kusatsu Line.
days.startLightGuidance: No hurry: the Tehara hotel does not check in until 18:00. Ask about leaving the bag earlier.
days.sleepBaseNote: Check-in 18:00 to midnight only. JR Tehara Station is about 150 m off the road.
days.tiredDaySummary: About 11 mi, flat, train alongside the whole way. Check-in not until 6 p.m.

days.label: Walk 15 — Tehara to Sanjo Ohashi
days.plan: Tehara → Kusatsu-juku → Seta → Otsu → Sanjo Ohashi, Kyoto.
days.terrain: Flat to Otsu along Biwa, then the final climb into Kyoto.
days.startLightGuidance: Rail-dense the whole way, and the whole point of the trip is at the end of it. Nov 7 is still free if the day needs splitting.
days.tiredDaySummary: About 19 mi into Kyoto. Rail all the way if needed.
